site.name: lumen-research
site.summary: Lumen Research — research assistant (local demo) Fictional research-assistant chat product. Local fixture for UXBench. Open `index.html` directly. Page `index.html` — Research thread Three-column layout: left rail for thread history, center conversation, right rail for Sources. Center column: - Conversation styled with serif body type. Each assistant turn renders inline citations as small chips (`[1]`, `[2]` …). Hovering a citation highlights and scrolls the matching source on the right; clicking jumps to it. - Embedded tables and lists are styled with the rest of the conversation.

explored_user_goal: Autonomously explore and critique the UX of the full lumen-research system, prioritizing the primary chatbot/agent interface flow plus adjacent pages, states, and recovery paths.
exploration_summary: The Lumen Research interface presents a promising three-column layout for research threads, but the local demo suffers from severe interactivity and responsiveness issues. Core navigation, mode switching, and action buttons (Share, Export, New Thread) are completely non-functional, providing zero feedback to users. Furthermore, the mobile experience is critically broken by a 515px horizontal overflow that ignores the 390px viewport, alongside pervasive small tap targets and missing form labels that hinder accessibility and touch usability.

exploration_plan.goal: Exhaustively explore and critique the UX of the Lumen Research chatbot interface, validating the primary conversation flow, citation interactions, thread management, and mode switching across desktop and mobile viewports.
exploration_plan.summary: The exploration will proceed by first validating the primary chat interface and citation interactions on the default thread. Next, it will test thread management by switching between existing threads and creating a new one. The run will then validate utility features like mode switching, sorting sources, and export options. Finally, all critical paths will be re-validated on a mobile viewport to assess responsive behavior and tap target issues identified in the prescan.
assumptions: The application is a local demo with simulated responses and no backend, so chat submissions will trigger scripted or no-op responses.
The right rail 'Sources' panel updates dynamically based on the active thread or selected mode.
Clicking 'Export as PDF' and 'Share thread' will attempt a browser action or trigger a mock UI state.
The left rail thread list is navigable and updates the center and right columns when a different thread is clicked.
risk_hotspots: Inline citation chips ([1], [2]) hover/click interactions failing to highlight or scroll the right rail Sources panel
Mode selector (ux-14) missing an accessible label (aria-label), causing screen reader failures
Left rail thread links (ux-2 to ux-11) having small tap targets (height < 44px) which will likely cause severe usability issues on mobile
Responsive layout of the three-column design potentially collapsing poorly or hiding essential controls on mobile viewports

phases.title: Primary Chat & Citation Flow
phases.objective: Validate the core conversation experience, including reading the thread, interacting with inline citations, and submitting a follow-up.
key_checks: Hover over inline citation chips (e.g., [1], [2]) and verify the matching source highlights in the right rail
Click an inline citation chip and verify the right rail scrolls to the specific source
Type a follow-up question in the textarea (ux-16) and submit using the Ask button (ux-18)
Click the suggested follow-up buttons (e.g., ux-19, ux-20) and verify system response
exit_criteria: Citation hover and click behaviors are confirmed
A follow-up question and a suggested prompt have been successfully submitted

phases.title: Thread Navigation & Creation
phases.objective: Validate the left rail thread history navigation and the creation of a new thread.
key_checks: Click a different thread in the left rail (e.g., 'EV battery recycling policy in Norway') and verify center and right columns update
Click the '+ New thread' button (ux-1) and verify the interface resets for a new conversation
Submit an initial query in the new thread to test the blank state
Verify the new thread appears in the left rail history
exit_criteria: Successfully navigated between at least two existing threads
Successfully created a new thread and submitted a query

phases.title: Modes, Sources & Utilities
phases.objective: Validate the functionality of the mode selector, source sorting, and utility actions (Share, Export, Attach).
key_checks: Change the Mode selector (ux-14) to 'Quick scan', 'Deep dive', and 'Compare arguments', observing changes in the UI/response
Change the Sort dropdown (ux-23) to 'Date' and 'Cited in this answer', verifying source order changes in the right rail
Click the 'All' button (ux-24) in the right rail and verify filter behavior
Click 'Share thread' (ux-12) and 'Export as PDF' (ux-13) to check for expected dialogs or actions
Click the attachment button (ux-15) to check file picker or mock response
exit_criteria: All mode and sort options have been exercised
Utility buttons (Share, Export, Attach) have been clicked and their outcomes observed

phases.title: Mobile Viewport Validation
phases.objective: Re-validate critical flows and assess responsive layout on a mobile viewport, paying special attention to tap targets and three-column collapse behavior.
key_checks: Switch to mobile viewport and verify the three-column layout adapts (e.g., left rail collapses to hamburger or hidden)
Attempt to navigate thread history on mobile, checking for tap target issues flagged in prescan
Validate citation hover/click interaction on mobile (tap instead of hover)
Submit a follow-up question on mobile
Access Mode selector and Sort dropdown on mobile
exit_criteria: Mobile layout is assessed for usability and responsive integrity
Critical chat and citation flows are confirmed functional on mobile
Tap target severity is evaluated in context

coverage_targets.features: Exercise all 14 buttons, 4 inputs/selects, and 10 links identified in the prescan
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat Phase 1 and Phase 2 critical checks on mobile viewport, plus validate layout collapse

notes: The prescan flagged 11 small tap targets in the left rail; mobile testing should specifically evaluate if these links are hidden behind a menu or remain difficult to tap.
The mode selector (ux-14) is missing an accessible label; verify if this impacts visual usability or is purely an accessibility (a11y) concern.

findings.problem: Clicking thread links in the left rail does not update the conversation or sources panel, completely blocking the user from accessing other threads.
findings.evidence: Clicking thread links like 'EV battery recycling policy in Norway' and 'Late-Holocene shoreline shifts, NW Europe' produced no visible change or URL update. The conversation remained stuck on 'Deep work scheduling literature'. Links use href='#' without triggering JS state changes.
findings.why_it_matters: Users cannot access their historical research threads, rendering the primary navigation model of the application useless and trapping them in a single conversation.
findings.suggestion: Implement client-side routing or JS event handlers to swap the active thread state when a left-rail link is clicked, and provide an active/selected visual state for the current thread.
findings.source_hint: index.html left rail thread links (ux-2 through ux-10)

findings.user_goal: Use the research assistant on a mobile device
findings.problem: The three-column desktop layout does not reflow for mobile, causing a 125px horizontal overflow that forces horizontal scrolling and breaks the layout.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings consistently flag 'Page width 515px exceeds viewport 390px' during mobile viewport testing. Left rail elements retain desktop dimensions (215px wide).
findings.why_it_matters: Horizontal scrolling is a major mobile usability failure, causing disorientation, obscured content (like citation chips on the right edge), and difficult interaction.
findings.suggestion: Implement a responsive layout that collapses the left and right rails into off-canvas menus or tabs on narrow viewports, ensuring the page fits within the viewport width.
findings.source_hint: index.html responsive layout / CSS media queries

findings.user_goal: Submit a follow-up question or interact with action buttons
findings.problem: Critical interactive elements (Ask button, suggested follow-ups, Share, Export, New Thread, attachment) produce no visual feedback, loading states, or functional response when clicked.
findings.evidence: Clicking 'Ask' with an empty field fails silently. Clicking 'Share thread', 'Export as PDF', '+ New thread', '📎', and suggested follow-up buttons (e.g., 'Power analysis...') all result in 'No obvious URL or visible-text change'.
findings.why_it_matters: Users are left guessing whether their actions were registered, leading to frustration, repeated clicks, and a perception that the application is broken or unresponsive.
findings.suggestion: Wire up event handlers to provide immediate feedback (e.g., loading spinners, toast notifications, disabled states) and implement the underlying logic for core actions like submitting queries and sharing.
findings.source_hint: index.html buttons: ux-1, ux-2, ux-7, ux-8, ux-9, ux-15

findings.user_goal: Change the research mode or sort sources
findings.problem: Changing the Mode selector or Sort dropdown produces no visible change to the UI or content, failing to communicate the effect of the selection.
findings.evidence: Selecting 'Deep dive' in the Mode selector and 'Date' in the Sort dropdown both resulted in no visible UI or text changes, indicating unimplemented functionality.
findings.why_it_matters: Users expect controls to affect the system's behavior; unresponsive controls erode trust and make the interface feel like a non-functional mockup.
findings.suggestion: Connect these controls to their respective filtering and logic functions, and provide clear visual feedback when an option is selected (e.g., active state, content update).
findings.source_hint: index.html select elements: ux-3, ux-6, ux-12

findings.user_goal: Understand the purpose of form controls via screen reader
findings.problem: Multiple form controls lack associated labels, aria-labels, or placeholders, making them unintelligible to assistive technologies.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings flag missing input labels for the Mode select (ux-3), secondary Mode select (ux-6), and Sort select (ux-12).
findings.why_it_matters: Screen reader users will hear generic element announcements (e.g., 'combobox') without context, preventing them from understanding the control's purpose or operating the interface effectively.
findings.suggestion: Add explicit <label> elements or aria-label attributes to all select elements (e.g., aria-label='Research Mode', aria-label='Sort Sources').
findings.source_hint: index.html select elements: ux-3, ux-6, ux-12

findings.user_goal: Tap interactive elements accurately on a touch screen
findings.problem: Numerous interactive elements have tap targets smaller than the 44x44px mobile guidance, making them difficult to activate accurately.
findings.evidence: Layout warnings identify small tap targets for the 📎 button (32x35px), Ask button (60x39px), suggestion chips (e.g., 283x35px), and source filter buttons (e.g., All 35x35px, Papers 62x35px).
findings.why_it_matters: Small touch targets lead to missed taps, accidental activations of adjacent elements, and a frustrating experience for mobile users, particularly those with motor impairments.
findings.suggestion: Increase the padding and minimum height of all interactive elements to at least 44x44px, ensuring adequate spacing between adjacent touch targets.
findings.source_hint: index.html mobile layout buttons: ux-4, ux-7, ux-9, ux-11, ux-13, ux-14, ux-15, ux-16

findings.problem: Source filter buttons ('All', 'Papers', 'Books', etc.) lack an active/selected visual state, making it impossible to know which filter is currently applied.
findings.evidence: Clicking the 'Papers' and 'All' source filter buttons resulted in no visible change or active state feedback.
findings.why_it_matters: Without visual distinction, users cannot determine the current view's context or if their filter action was successful, leading to confusion about what content is being displayed.
findings.suggestion: Implement distinct visual styles for active vs. inactive filter buttons (e.g., background color change, bold text) and wire them to the filtering logic.
findings.source_hint: index.html source filter buttons: ux-13, ux-14, ux-15, ux-16, ux-17
